title: Fractions of a lap on the running track

blocks.text: Today you and the learner put fractions on a running track. A runner stops part way round, and the lap is cut into equal parts.
The learner has met halves, thirds and quarters as equal parts of one whole.

blocks.do: Show the oval track cut into equal parts.
blocks.say: The whole lap is one. Each mark cuts it into equal parts.
blocks.why: Seeing the lap split makes the bottom number of the fraction concrete.

blocks.do: Point to where the runner stops.
blocks.say: The runner has gone this many parts out of the whole lap.
blocks.why: The runner's spot is the top number of the fraction.

blocks.title: What only you can do
items: Watch whether the learner counts the parts or guesses by distance.
Ask them to trace the runner's path with a finger first.

blocks.title: A step ahead
blocks.body: If this feels easy, ask what one more part would make.
blocks.prompt: How far round is the runner, as a fraction of the lap?

blocks.q: What if they count the marks, not the parts between them?
blocks.a: Count the gaps the runner crosses, not the lines.

more.q: What if two runners confuse them?
more.a: Cover one lane and read the other on its own first.

more.q: What if they still are not sure?
more.a: Drop back to one runner on one lane and count parts out loud.

blocks.text: Note whether counting parts or comparing distance worked better for this learner.

blocks.title: A step ahead
blocks.body: After you read the lap, try adding one more part in your head.

blocks.title: A lap on the track
blocks.ask_learner: Which runner has gone further round the lap?
blocks.why: Three quarters is further round than two quarters, so the first runner leads.

blocks.title: Adding two parts of a lap
blocks.ask_learner: Does the runner finish before or past one full lap?
blocks.why: Three quarters plus two thirds is more than one, so the runner passes the finish into a second lap.

mistakes.count-lines: Counts the marks instead of the parts between them.
mistakes.far-wins: Thinks the lane drawn on the outside is always further.

items.q: A lap is cut into four equal parts and the runner is on the third mark. How far round is that?

choices.text: Whichever lane is on the outside.

items.explain: Three parts out of four equal parts is three quarters.

blocks.q: How do I read a runner on the track?
blocks.a: Count how many equal parts the runner has passed out of the whole lap.

more.q: What if two runners are close?
more.a: Read each lane on its own, then compare the two fractions.

more.q: What if I am still stuck?
more.a: Count the parts on one lane out loud from the start line.
